messages.content: Idaho is wrapped. Nashville just turned into a real trip. I need a flight and hotel shortlist for the water-tech conference.
Sure. Give me the conference dates, when you need to be at the convention center, and whether the return is fixed or still moving.

Conference runs Monday through Wednesday, Nov. 18 to 20. They want me there for Monday morning booth setup, and I’m on a partner panel sometime Monday. Sessions end Wednesday around 3:30. There may be a vendor dinner Wednesday night, so Thursday return is possible.
Understood. For the outbound, should I search SFO only, or include Oakland and San Jose if the timing is materially better?
SFO first, but OAK is fine if it gives me a clean nonstop. SJC only if it is clearly better. Coach is fine. Keep it to one stop max and not some long airport sit.
Got it. Any preferred arrival target on Sunday?

Badge check-in closes around 8:30 Sunday night. I’d like to stop at the convention center, then still have an hour to clean up slides at the hotel. Afternoon departure would be ideal if that doesn’t make Nashville too late.
That points to a Sunday departure that lands before roughly 7:15 p.m. at BNA. I’ll keep the layover options short and compare against any nonstop from OAK.

For hotels, compare the official block against a nearby downtown option. Keep the guest rating around 4.0 or better. I’m not interested in a tired block hotel just because it’s official. Easy dinner matters.
I’ll screen out the weak reviews and call out restaurant access. If room amenities are listed, I’ll note coffee maker and mini-fridge availability too.
Good. What do the flights look like?

Flight shortlist: best schedule fit is Southwest OAK-BNA nonstop Sunday 12:55 p.m. to 6:55 p.m., with a Wednesday 5:20 p.m. BNA-OAK nonstop return. It protects badge check-in and slide time, but seats are not assigned. United from SFO via Houston is acceptable: 12:40 p.m. to 8:38 p.m. with about a 75-minute connection, then Wednesday BNA-DEN-SFO around 5:05 p.m. to 10:30 p.m.; cleaner for assigned seats and loyalty, but the Sunday arrival is late. Delta via Salt Lake is a backup, 11:25 a.m. to 6:58 p.m.; decent timing, but it leaves earlier and still connects.
Can you compare Wednesday versus Thursday without locking me into Thursday yet?

Yes. Wednesday return works if you can leave the convention center by 3:45 and skip the vendor dinner: Southwest nonstop at 5:20 gives the cleanest exit; United’s one-stop is similar departure time but lands later in SF. Thursday gives breathing room after dinner: Southwest has a late-morning nonstop back to OAK, while United has a midmorning one-stop through Denver or Houston. Best tactic is to wait on the dinner and teardown assignment before buying a less flexible return.
Okay. Hotels?

Hotel shortlist: the official headquarters block is the Omni Nashville, attached or effectively adjacent to Music City Center. Block rate is showing about $289 before taxes, guest feedback around 4.3, with good convention convenience but recent comments about elevator waits and crowded lobby service. On-site restaurants are good; in-room fridge looks request-based, not guaranteed. The stronger downtown alternative is Hyatt Centric Downtown Nashville, about two blocks from the convention center, rating around 4.6, with listed in-room coffee maker and small fridge, plus on-site dining and many SoBro/Fifth and Broadway restaurants nearby. Rate is showing around $279 refundable, but I would check the company portal before treating that as final.
Is the official hotel worth the convenience?

Only if you expect to be running back and forth for booth materials. For booth setup alone, the attached hotel is convenient but not decisive. Hyatt Centric looks like the better stay for evenings and slide work, and it avoids the weaker block feedback. The trade-off is a short outdoor walk.
Any issue getting from BNA downtown on Sunday evening?

Not a major one. Normal rideshare or taxi is 15 to 25 minutes; with event traffic, plan 30 to 40. The OAK nonstop should put you downtown around 7:35 to 7:50, which still works. The United one-stop likely puts hotel arrival closer to 9:15, so badge check-in and slide review get compressed.
I’ll ask Michelle if she can cover Wednesday teardown, and I need to see whether our company rate beats the block. Don’t book yet. Rank what you’d hold.

Ranked hold: best fit is the OAK-BNA Sunday nonstop, Hyatt Centric Downtown, and a Wednesday evening nonstop return if Michelle covers teardown. It gives the cleanest Sunday arrival and the better-rated hotel with easier dinner options. Acceptable backup is United SFO-Houston-BNA plus the Omni block if the company pushes SFO or you need to be attached to the convention center. I would ask before booking the return until Michelle confirms teardown and the vendor dinner, and ask before booking the hotel until the company rate is checked against the block.

messages.content: Update on Nashville: panel moved to Monday at 8:30 a.m., the booth crate is supposed to arrive Sunday evening, and the official hotel block reviews are not inspiring.
That makes Sunday arrival more important. Are you personally responsible for receiving the crate, or just checking that it made it to the booth before Monday morning?
Not officially receiving it. The freight company delivers to the booth. I just need to make sure it isn’t missing. Michelle might cover Wednesday teardown, but she hasn’t confirmed.

Then the earlier nonstop is the better flight. Southwest OAK-BNA Sunday about 12:55 to 6:55 should get you downtown around 7:40. The United SFO-Houston-BNA option lands closer to 8:40, so the crate check and slide review get squeezed.
OAK is acceptable. Any reason to use SFO instead?

Only if assigned seating, MileagePlus credit, or easier ground logistics from home outweigh the Sunday timing. For this schedule, the OAK nonstop is cleaner. The United one-stop is an acceptable backup, not the best fit.
Hotel choice is down to the connected official hotel versus Hyatt Centric two blocks away. The official place looks convenient but tired.

Hyatt Centric fits better if you can handle a 6 to 8 minute walk. It is better rated, lists a small fridge and coffee maker, has an on-site restaurant, and has plenty of nearby dinner options. The connected hotel wins only for bad weather, gear runs, or if you expect constant booth back-and-forth.
Do I lose much for the 8:30 panel by not staying connected?

Not much. If you check the crate Sunday night and leave the hotel by about 7:35 Monday, you have time for the walk, badge scan, and panel room setup. I would not choose the weaker block hotel just for that panel time.
Return plan: keep Wednesday unless I’m stuck with teardown. Vendor dinner is maybe sixty percent.

Best structure is fixed outbound Sunday, hotel with a refundable Wednesday night if the cancellation terms are reasonable, and a return held as Wednesday evening until Michelle answers. If dinner and teardown firm up, shift to a Thursday late-morning return instead of rushing.
Don’t book until Michelle answers and we know if the corporate rate beats the block.

Understood. I will not book. Current rank: best fit is OAK-BNA nonstop Sunday, Hyatt Centric Downtown, and Wednesday evening return if Michelle handles teardown. Acceptable backup is United one-stop from SFO plus the connected hotel only if you need the attached location or assigned-seat loyalty tradeoff. Ask-before-booking items are Michelle on teardown, the vendor dinner, and Hyatt corporate rate versus the official block.
